summary.text: James Byrd is a former Wyoming state representative and professional geophysicist running as the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. A fifth-generation Wyomingite from Cheyenne, he served ten years in the Wyoming House, including as a Democratic leader. He says he is running on an independent approach focused on working families' costs, rural health care, and public lands.

paragraphs.text: Describes himself as a fifth-generation Wyomingite; earned a high school diploma from Cheyenne Central High School and attended Laramie County Community College and the University of Wyoming.
His mother, Liz Byrd, was Wyoming's first Black state senator, and his father, Jim Byrd, was the state's first Black police chief, according to his candidate survey.

Worked as a security consultant, computer network designer, exploration geophysicist (including for Compagnie Generale de Geophysique and Amoco/BP), and contract computer project manager for firms including American Express and Cargill.
Served ten years in the Wyoming House of Representatives, District 44, from 2009 to 2019, winning re-election in 2012 and later cycles.

In the legislature, served as Minority Whip from 2013 to 2015 and was elected Minority Caucus Leader in 2015; his committees included Corporations, Elections and Political Subdivisions and Minerals, Business and Economic Development.
Advanced from the 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, defeating Billy Benavidez.
